sec1.titulo: The question you did not ask
abertura: In the lesson you are going to ask your teacher a lot of questions, and find out three things you did not know.
Three of the sentences below are true. Mark those three.

itens.t: A question keeps a conversation going better than an answer does.
itens.porque: An answer can end. A question hands the turn back and buys you the whole time the other person takes.

itens.t: If you are not sure your question is correct, it is better not to ask it.
itens.porque: A question with the words in the wrong order still gets answered. A question nobody asks gets nothing.

itens.t: The best question is usually the second one, about the answer you just heard.
itens.porque: Anyone can ask what they prepared. The second one proves you were listening, and it is the one you will practice in the lesson.

itens.t: You need to know a lot of words to ask a good question.
itens.porque: Why? is one word. Most of the questions that matter are five words long.

itens.t: Short answers force you to ask again.
itens.porque: This is on purpose in the last part of the lesson: your teacher answers short so that you have to keep going.

itens.t: Asking a lot of questions makes you look like you did not understand.
itens.porque: It makes you look interested. The person who is lost is the one who stops asking.

sec1.pt: Na aula você vai fazer muitas perguntas e descobrir três coisas que não sabia. Antes disso, marque as três frases verdadeiras sobre perguntas.

nota.titulo: Por que uma aula inteira sobre perguntar
nota.texto: Você já começa conversas sozinha. Perguntar é o que faz elas continuarem — e é a única coisa nesta aula que não depende de você saber o assunto.

sec2.pt: Seis palavras da semana de escola. Escolha o sentido que cabe. Você vai usar essas palavras na aula, nas perguntas que fizer.

nota.titulo: Seis palavras que servem esta semana
nota.texto: Todas as seis são coisas sobre as quais você fala em português todo dia. Vocabulário do que já acontece com você é o que volta sozinho quando você precisa — e é isso que faltava.

abertura: Read each line out loud, and decide what it is. Do not change anything — just say which one it is.

itens.t: You are in the last year.
itens.porque: Nothing is asked. Two words in, you already know it is telling you something.

itens.t: Are you in the last year?
itens.porque: The same five words, in a different order. Only two of them changed places.

itens.t: She handed in the group work.
itens.porque: It reports something that happened, and nobody is waiting for an answer.

itens.t: Did she hand in the group work?
itens.porque: A word arrived at the front that was not in the statement at all. Notice which one.
It gives information. Said with a rising voice it could be a question, and written like this it is not.
It starts with a question word, and the order after it is still not the order of the statement.

sec3.rationale: Read the three pairs one after the other. Something moves between the statement and the question every single time, and it is always the same kind of word.
sec3.pt: Leia cada linha em voz alta e decida: é uma pergunta ou uma afirmação? Não mude nada — só diga o que é.

sec4.titulo: A notice on the school wall

doc.texto:
Groups of three. You choose your own group.
Hand in the written part by Friday 14, before the end of the school day. Late work loses ten per cent.
You present in the last week of the month. Ten minutes each group, and everyone in the group speaks.
Questions? Come and find me at the second break, not by email.

abertura: Three of these are true. Mark those three.

itens.t: You can choose who you work with.
itens.porque: You choose your own group. It is one short line and it is the one everybody reads first.

itens.t: You can hand the written part in on Saturday and lose nothing.
itens.porque: The deadline is Friday, and late work loses ten per cent. Handing in late is allowed and it is not free.

itens.t: Every person in the group has to speak.
itens.porque: everyone in the group speaks. It changes who you want in your group, which is why it is in the notice.

itens.t: The presentation is on the same day as the written part.
itens.porque: Friday 14 for the writing, the last week of the month for the presentation. Two dates, and the notice never says they are the same.

itens.t: If you have a question, you have to ask in person.
itens.porque: Come and find me at the second break, not by email. That is the whole reason a lesson about asking questions is useful.

itens.t: There is no limit on how long you present.
itens.porque: Ten minutes per group. The number is easy to miss because it is in the middle of a longer line.

sec4.pt: Leia o aviso de trabalho em grupo e marque as três frases verdadeiras. É o tipo de texto que você lê na parede da escola — e em inglês ele é exatamente igual.

abertura: Choose the ending that belongs there. All six words from activity two are in here somewhere.
sec5.pt: Cada frase começa de um jeito. Escolha o final que combina. As seis palavras do exercício 2 estão aqui dentro.

abertura: Write six questions you would ask your teacher about their week.

callout.texto:
Write them the way they come out. In the lesson you will ask these same six out loud before anything is explained, and you will look at them again at the end.

Two about the weekend, two about work, and two about anything you actually want to know.

sec6.pt:
Escreva seis perguntas que você faria à professora sobre a semana dela. Duas sobre o fim de semana, duas sobre o trabalho, e duas sobre qualquer coisa que você queira saber de verdade.

Nada aqui é corrigido: escreva do jeito que sair. Na aula você vai fazer essas mesmas seis perguntas em voz alta, antes de qualquer explicação.

itens.porque: Are is in front of you. In the statement it would be behind it: you are new here.
This is the statement with a question mark on the end. People do say it, with a surprised voice — and it means something else: I cannot believe it.
Did comes in front of you, and choose goes back to its plain form. Two things happened at once here.
Nothing moved and nothing arrived. It is understandable, and it is the single most common way this goes wrong.
There was no auxiliary in you know anyone here, so do arrived to be one. That is the whole job it has.
Did is in the right place and the past is marked twice. English marks it once: did you choose.

gd21.rationale: Look at the three that are wrong. Two of them forgot to move anything; the third moved the word and kept the past on the verb as well.

itens.porque: Are comes before you. Say the statement out loud right after and you will hear them swap.
Same two words, other way round. This is the only difference between telling and asking here.

itens.t: Did she hand in the group work?
itens.porque: Did before she. And the main verb is hand, not handed — the past is already in did.
The question word comes first, and then the same swap happens behind it: is before your deadline.
This is the exception, and the next screen is about it. Who is the person doing the sitting, so there is nothing to swap it with.

itens.t: She can help you with the deadline.
itens.porque: Can after she. Turn it into a question and it is the only word that has to move.

aux21.rationale: Four questions, two statements, and one exception. In every question but one, the little word is in front of the subject — and that is the whole rule.

itens.porque: Who is the person doing the wanting. There is no other subject to put an auxiliary in front of.
What is the thing that happened. Same case as who sits over there, and the reason there is no did.
Here who is not doing the talking — she is. So the auxiliary comes back and goes in front of her.
You is doing the choosing, so did is needed. Compare it with what happened and the difference is who does the action.
The people are the ones who came. The question word is the subject, so nothing moves.

itens.t: How many people did you invite?
itens.porque: The people did not invite anybody — you did. As soon as there is another subject, the auxiliary is back.

wh21.rationale: Ask yourself one thing on each: is the question word the one doing the action? If it is, nothing moves. If somebody else is doing it, the auxiliary comes in.

alts: do you work on a Monday?
do you works on a Monday?
itens.ok: do you work on a Monday?

alts: do you are doing this weekend?

abertura: One rule, one exception, and six questions you can use tomorrow.

tabela: The auxiliary goes in front of the subject: Are you…? Can she…? Did you…?
do, does or did comes in to be one: you know → do you know?
Did you choose?, never did you chose. The past is already in did.
When the question word is the one doing the action, nothing moves: Who sits there? What happened?

callout.texto: You asked six questions before anyone explained anything, and at the end of the hour you looked at them again and could see which ones you would say differently. You did the explaining; the screen only confirmed it.

abertura: Record a short voice message, if you would like to.

callout.texto:
Someone new joins your class tomorrow and you are the person who talks to them first.

What you are trying to do: ask them five questions, out loud, one after the other, without writing them down first.

lista: anything you would actually want to know

speakmore.pt:
Grave um recado curto de voz, se quiser. É opcional: nada aqui é corrigido nem cobrado na próxima aula.

A situação: alguém novo entra na sua turma amanhã e você é a primeira pessoa a falar com essa pessoa. Faça cinco perguntas, em voz alta, uma atrás da outra, sem escrever antes.

abertura: Write six questions for someone you would like to interview: a person you admire, someone in your family, anybody.

callout.texto:
Three of the six have to be questions about an answer — the kind you can only ask once the other person has said something.

Write the answer you imagine first, and then the question it would produce.

writemore.pt:
Escreva seis perguntas para alguém que você gostaria de entrevistar: uma pessoa que você admira, alguém da sua família, qualquer um.

A parte difícil: três das seis têm de ser perguntas sobre uma resposta — do tipo que só dá para fazer depois que a pessoa falou. Escreva primeiro a resposta que você imagina, e depois a pergunta que ela produziria.
